yarn.meaning: Every point survives, including the strategic/practical balance and the open, iterative, user-centred commitment ("takes it a step at a time, and is built around the people who'll use it"). "doing work that'll fair knock your socks off" shifts "inspiring" toward "astonishing".
yarn.sense: Mostly exact ("fired up", "top-notch", "give us a yell", "delivering the goods"). "fair knock your socks off" for "inspiring" strains a little; "give a stuff" is usually heard in the negative.
yarn.authenticity: Sounds like an Australian manager writing: "a cracker of a crew", "makes or breaks", "We're stoked to have you".
yarn.register: Heavier than level 3: an added "G'day, and welcome aboard", and nearly every line retold in slang ("cracker of a crew", "fair knock your socks off", "give a stuff"). "give a stuff" is mild, within vulgarity 1.
yarn.tone: Keeps the warm, upbeat welcome; a touch more matey than the original's polished tone.
yarn.flow: Reads smoothly, though "a modern, pitch-in-together, all-sorts-welcome culture" is a hyphenated pile-up.
yarn.variety: Varied: "cracker", "fired up", "give a stuff", "top-notch", "makes or breaks", "dead set", "give us a yell", "stoked".
yarn.essence: Unmistakably the TTS welcome letter, retold.

engine.meaning: The original almost verbatim. "a remarkable group of battlers" recasts talented staff as people doing it tough.
engine.sense: "battlers" takes the wrong sense for skilled colleagues; "bloody great partner" and "our bloody organisation" put an intensifier where none fits.
engine.authenticity: The Aussie is bolted on: "our bloody organisation", "dead set on" dropped into formal prose; US "user-centered" left in.
engine.register: Almost entirely untranslated, well below level 3; "bloody" is within vulgarity 1 but it is most of the Aussie there is.
engine.tone: "our bloody organisation" sounds exasperated in a warm welcome.
engine.flow: Stiff where the swaps land: "We are dead set on working in an open, iterative and user-centered way".
engine.variety: Leans on "bloody" twice and little else.
engine.essence: Recognisably the letter, because it is the letter.

unharnessed.meaning: Every point survives, close to the original: "We're committed to working in an open, iterative and user-centred way, with a strong focus on delivery."
unharnessed.sense: Mostly exact ("ripper bunch", "fired up", "top-notch", "give us a yell"). "show off the modern, collaborative, diverse culture" for "exemplify" strains: showing off implies boasting.
unharnessed.authenticity: Natural: "a ripper bunch of people", "We're stoked to have you on the TTS team". "bloody talented" sits well.
unharnessed.register: Right weight for level 3: retold in a relaxed Australian voice with a steady few terms, the formal bones kept. "bloody" is within vulgarity 1.
unharnessed.tone: Keeps the warm, upbeat, professional welcome.
unharnessed.flow: Reads smoothly, like it was written that way.
unharnessed.variety: Varied for its length: "ripper", "seriously", "fired up", "bloody", "top-notch", "nimble", "give us a yell", "stoked".
